anomalies.description: A soldier fires a sniper rifle, producing a visible dust cloud and recoil at the muzzle, confirming discharge of the weapon.
A sudden dust and debris plume erupts from the lower portion of a cinderblock wall, indicating a nearby explosion or impact.

A soldier is in prone position with a sniper rifle mounted on a bipod, aiming through the scope; muzzle flash and recoil are not visible, but the sustained aiming posture and context (immediately after explosion) strongly indicate active engagement/shooting.
A rifle is fired; visible muzzle flash and recoil motion in frame f4, followed by dust disturbance at the firing position in f5.

A bullet casing is ejected upward (f8–f9), then impacts the ground (f10), causing a small localized explosion/dust burst upon impact (f11–f15). The sequence shows the casing falling, striking the ground, and ejecting debris—consistent with a high-velocity impact explosion.
A bullet casing is ejected and strikes the ground, causing a visible dust impact and rebound; this is consistent with a firearm discharge captured in slow motion.

A soldier is shown aiming a rifle with a scope; the subsequent frame (f10) shows a distant figure in a window, consistent with a targeting sequence, and the rapid camera shift suggests recoil or immediate follow-up action typical of a shot being fired.

The figure in the window (f11–f14) appears to flinch or recoil abruptly between f11 and f12, suggesting impact from a projectile; this occurs after the shooter’s aim is established and aligns temporally with a likely shot.
